theme: 3 terms on where code lives and who can reach it: a unit of code you import, hiding code inside one file, and letting other modules subclass a class

terms.definition: A unit of code, such as an app or a framework, that you build and import as one piece.
terms.example: `Payments` is its own Module, so add `import Payments` at the top.

terms.definition: A keyword that hides a declaration from all code outside its own source file.
terms.example: I made `limit` Fileprivate, so only this file can read it.

terms.definition: A keyword that lets other modules use a class and also subclass it and override its methods.
terms.example: Mark `Screen` Open, or the app can't subclass it.

quizzes.question: What keyword lets another module subclass your class and override its methods?

video.title: Module, Fileprivate & Open | Day 36
video.description:
Learn to explain modules and the last two access levels in Swift: Module, Fileprivate & Open, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Module - A unit of code, such as an app or a framework, that you build and import as one piece.
Fileprivate - A keyword that hides a declaration from all code outside its own source file.
Open - A keyword that lets other modules use a class and also subclass it and override its methods.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Module - A unit of code, such as an app or a framework, that you build and import as one piece.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these access terms in English?

dialogue.title: Why is CardView Open?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why did you mark `CardView` Open? Isn't Public enough?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The app target is a different Module, and it needs to subclass `CardView`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So Public lets another Module use the class, but not subclass it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Open also lets the app override methods like `tap()`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. And why is `maxCards` Fileprivate? I wanted to read it in my other file.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the point. Only code in this file can read it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait, isn't that what Private does?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Close. Private hides it outside the type. Fileprivate hides it outside the file.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. Does every method need Open, or just the class?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every method too. Without it, the app can call `tap()`, but not override it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Fileprivate for one file, Open for subclasses in another Module.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a separate Module. Import it first.
